text: Risk management is a vital process for any business. It begins with identifying potential risks, which could range from financial issues to natural disasters. Once identified, companies develop mitigation strategies to reduce the likelihood or impact of these risks. For example, a company might diversify its suppliers to avoid disruption. However, not all risks can be eliminated, so contingency plans are essential. These are pre-arranged actions to take if a risk materializes, ensuring the business can continue operating. Finally, effective risk management requires constant monitoring. By regularly reviewing risks and plans, companies can adapt to new threats and stay prepared for an uncertain future.
